sentences.text: Dianosuchus possessed conical, isodont teeth that lacked striations, alongside very small antorbital fenestrae, which are openings in the skull.
This reptile lived during the Sinemurian stage of the Early Jurassic, between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago.
Young described the species Dianosuchus changchiawaensis in 1982 based on fossils found in the Dark Red Beds of the Lower Lufeng Formation in Yunnan, China.
The animal belongs to the genus Dianosuchus and is a member of the family Protosuchidae, classifying it as a reptile.
Fossils date to the Sinemurian stage of the Early Jurassic, placing the animal's life between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago in Yunnan, China.
